corrected_value.title: Differences between left- and right-handers in approach/avoidance motivation: influence of consistency of handedness measures.

decisions.quote: Our results replicate those of Wright et al. (2009) and Hardie and Wright (2014) that left-handers have higher BIS scores than right-handers while, as expected, there is no handedness difference for any BAS sub-scale.
decisions.location: Independent parent primary-source context; exhausted_candidate_0029.parent.json raw offsets
decisions.reason: Parent independently inspected prediction, new N86 sample, own Discussion and exact Hardie/Wright2014reference. Current authors explicitly replicate its handedness-direction finding and separately test/contrast its N689handedness-consistency/strength finding using comparable classifications. Shipped Wright/Hardie/Wilson2009N110is a different empirical study and lacks that later consistency finding; this is not a year/DOI-only difference or a duplicate report. New identity-only outcome remains unknown.
